message.content: In lions, one of the most striking dominant genetic traits is **mane development in males**. The presence and size of the mane are controlled by genes that are expressed dominantly in male lions, meaning that even if only one copy of the relevant allele is present, the lion will develop a mane. This trait is linked to testosterone levels and is a key factor in male social status and mating success.
